comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch. See rule G100.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime, and the editor extensions this plugin registers would attach to the wrong one.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state — obsidian peer-pins it exactly. SelectionHighlightComponent's StateField/decorations must run against Obsidian's own CodeMirror instance.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: build:compile fails in obsidian-dev-utils' check-project-types (`sys`) and type-aware lint fails in @typescript-eslint (`ModuleKind`). @typescript-eslint peer-requires >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.

brace-expansion.why: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (high, DoS via unbounded expansion) covers brace-expansion <=5.0.7, and 18 vulnerable copies reach the tree transitively through old minimatch majors — eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-react on minimatch ^3.1.2, readdir-glob on ^5.1.0, eslint-plugin-json-schema-validator on ^8.0.0, eslint-plugin-n and glob on ^9.x. Nothing we depend on directly can be bumped to fix it, so the patched version is forced tree-wide instead. 5.0.8 is dual-published (exports.require -> dist/commonjs), so the old CJS minimatch copies still resolve it; verified with a clean lint run and the full unit suite.
